stem: A community health nurse is teaching household disaster preparedness. Which recommendation best reflects current FEMA Ready.gov guidance?

options.A: Keep only enough supplies for the first few hours because emergency services will always arrive immediately.
options.B: Maintain emergency supplies for several days and tailor the kit to household medical, disability, child, pet, and other unique needs.
options.C: Store only food; water, medicines, and communication supplies are unnecessary.
options.D: Use one identical kit for every household regardless of medical or functional needs.

rationale: FEMA Ready.gov recommends a basic emergency supply kit that can support the household for several days and emphasizes adapting the kit for individual household needs such as medications, disabilities, children, older adults, and pets.
educational_objective: Teach evidence-based household emergency-kit preparation using FEMA guidance.
source_document_title: Ready.gov — Build a Kit / National Preparedness Month Toolkit
source_version_date: Toolkit last updated 2025-08-26; current guidance rechecked 2026-08-17
source_locator: Build a Kit: supplies for several days; additional emergency supplies based on individual needs
source_claim_supported: Households should prepare several days of emergency supplies and tailor kits to individual medical and functional needs.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8/PDF p.12
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — disaster preparedness
correction_summary: Replaced vague preparedness advice with FEMA's current several-days and individualized-needs recommendations.
